alert.title: Three sample exceptions — prioritize by risk and evidence
alert.desc: Review an input-quality issue, a stale-feature baseline and an expected event. Each is a separate synthetic product group in the same example cycle.

exceptions.diagnosis: A simulated file-format change interrupted the Maplebridge Market sample feed. Review the missing observations before using this group.

alert.title: Missing observations make this group unreliable
alert.desc: A simulated file-format change interrupted the Maplebridge Market sample feed. Review the missing observations before using this group.

rca.finding: The synthetic cocoa gift boxes feed is missing four days of observations. A sample export renamed its quantity field; validation rejected the new format rather than ingesting misleading totals. This issue is confined to this feed group. The recommended next step is a mapping check and a reviewed backfill, followed by validation before releasing forecasts.
evidence: Example source: Maplebridge Market · last sample received 2026-04-20
Four synthetic daily files rejected because quantity_case changed to quantity_units.
Sample completeness score: 0.46; review threshold: 0.75.
Historical example DEMO-VL-01-H: the same validation pattern was resolved with a mapping correction.

actions.title: Flag the affected group
actions.desc: Flag the affected product group for a data-quality review.

actions.title: Review mapping and backfill
actions.desc: A specialist would confirm the unit conversion, backfill the four days, and validate totals.

actions.title: Escalate repeated schema changes
actions.desc: Engineering review would agree a versioned feed contract with the fictional supplier.

planner.cause: A changed sales file format interrupted the feed
planner.impact: Forecasts for this group are unreliable until the missing data is restored.
planner.diagnosis: This is a data problem, not a model problem. Correct the quantity mapping before using the forecast.
evidence: Maplebridge Market: four daily files rejected.
Data completeness: 46%, below the 75% threshold.
A similar historical case was resolved by correcting the mapping.
planner.recommendation: Check units, restore the four missing days, then validate totals.
planner.approval: A specialist must review the backfill before forecasts are released. Escalate repeated format changes to engineering.

exceptions.precedentSummary: Synthetic retail-format incident: a quantity column was renamed, causing validation failures. The mapping was corrected and missing files reprocessed. Data completeness was restored in the next cycle.

exceptions.diagnosis: The clean-feed group uses an outdated seasonal demand coefficient. Compare retraining with an interim correction.

alert.title: Stale features are shifting the forecast baseline
alert.desc: The clean-feed group uses an outdated seasonal demand coefficient. Compare retraining with an interim correction.

rca.finding: For this separate spring confectionery group, the sample feeds are complete. The seasonal demand coefficient has not been refreshed for ten weeks, and its drift score is 0.73 against a 0.55 review threshold. Synthetic demand exceeds forecasts across three successive cycles. A refreshed feature set and model retrain are recommended; a time-limited correction is proposed while the change is reviewed.
evidence: This group uses a separate validated feed: completeness 0.97 with no rejected files.
Synthetic feature: seasonal demand coefficient · drift 0.73 > 0.55.
Illustrative wMAPE: 8.6% → 10.4% → 12.7% across three cycles.
Underforecast bias (actual minus forecast, divided by actual): +0.06 → +0.10 → +0.15.
Historical example DEMO-VL-02-H supports refreshing the feature before retraining.

actions.title: Review retrain recommendation
actions.desc: Proposed model: demo_seasonal_v3. Refresh seasonal demand coefficient and compare a 16-month training window against the current baseline.

actions.title: Review interim correction
actions.desc: Proposed +11% correction for two cycles, with an explicit expiry and weekly review.

actions.title: Escalate missing refresh ownership
actions.desc: Agree who owns feature refreshes and who can approve future model changes. This recurring issue merits a tracked decision.

planner.impact: Underforecasting may leave plans short of demand.
planner.diagnosis: The input data is complete. Outdated model assumptions are driving the forecast shortfall.
evidence: Inputs are 97% complete; no rejected files.
Forecast error rose from 8.6% to 12.7% over three cycles.
Demand now exceeds the forecast by 15% of actual demand.
planner.recommendation: Refresh the inputs and retrain the model. Consider a temporary +11% adjustment for two cycles.
planner.approval: Human approval is required for retraining and the temporary adjustment. Assign an owner and an expiry before any change.

exceptions.precedentSummary: Historical case: a stale seasonal feature shifted the baseline. Refreshed inputs and a controlled model retrain improved wMAPE from 12.1% to 10.0% within two cycles.

exceptions.diagnosis: A registered promotion explains the +22% demand change. No corrective action is needed; monitor through the promotion window.

alert.title: The event uplift is expected; monitor through the promotion
alert.desc: A registered promotion explains the +22% demand change. No corrective action is needed; monitor through the promotion window.

rca.finding: This cocoa gift boxes event group has clean inputs, no material feature drift and no persistent model degradation. A registered promotion runs from 2026-04-27 through 2026-05-03. The +22% forecast change is within the historical 18–24% range. This is an expected demand signal, not a data or model failure. Monitor through the promotion and reassess only if actual demand materially diverges.
evidence: Event-group sample completeness: 1.00; no feed validation failures.
Synthetic calendar window: 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-03.
Example forecast delta: +22%; fictional historical range: +18–24%.
Monitoring review point: end of promotion window, 3 May 2026. No override or retraining required.

planner.issue: Forecast spike matches a planned event
planner.impact: The increase matches past promotions; monitor through the event window.
planner.diagnosis: The event explains the demand change. There is no evidence of a broken data feed.
evidence: Inputs are 100% complete; no feed failures.
Demand change: +22%, within the historical +18–24% range.
Event window: 27 April–3 May 2026.
planner.recommendation: No corrective action or approval required. Monitor forecast and actual demand through 3 May 2026; escalate only if actual demand materially diverges from the expected promotional range.
planner.approval: No approval required. Monitoring review point: 3 May 2026.
